non_primitives.reason: Format string write via %n is theoretically possible (FORTIFY disabled, %n available) if attacker can place a pointer to a string containing %n in the user buffer. However: (1) No format specifier strings exist in .rodata or .data sections of the binary. (2) The INFO_LEAK at counter=68 provides PIE base, but counter=69 crashes, preventing same-run use of the leaked address. (3) In a fork-server scenario, the leak could enable placing a known address containing %n bytes (e.g., searching .text or libc for 0x25 0x6e bytes), but this requires multi-step setup beyond single-BUG primitive scope. ARB_WRITE remains THEORETICAL at best and is not verified.
